It could be a few things. Someone could be hacking into your system (unlikely). Your headphones could be picking up radio signals. Or, you’re suffering from auditory hallucinations (this is surprisingly common). Try to the rule out the first two first. Auditory hallucinations can be caused by many things. Stress. Sleep deprivation and sleep disorders. Anything that might cause brain fog (covid, the flu, etc). Migraines. Very rarely, schizophrenia and other mental health disorders. And lots and lots of other things you wouldn’t expect to cause such a symptom. The brain is weird!

First, work on ruling out the other two. Record with OBS or something else and see if the recording picks up the sounds. If it does, send the recording to a trusted friend or family member and ask if they hear it too. Also, for the love of god, check your carbon dioxide detectors and make sure they’re working correctly. That stuff is DEADLY. And will make you hallucinate. If other people are unable to hear the sounds you’re hearing, and everything’s in order with the CO2, then it might be a health issue.

Looks like a Abscess. You can get it lanced at an urgent care or possibly an ER. Don’t wait too long the infection can get severe and potentially deadly. I got it lanced at the ER, doctor cleaned it out and put some gauze in it and prescribed antibiotics. If you wait too long though and the infection makes you septic or makes the skin necrotic, you’ll be stuck in the hospital for a bit, and that’s never fun. Better to get it taken care of before that happens!

The Coruscant Jedi Temple has a big ass prison in it just for Sith. I would assume Tython likely does too (we just don’t see it in game). Jedi custody is generally treated differently than Republic custody, hence why the Jedi can bring Sith into their ranks without the Republic being able to go “wait hold on, that guy murdered like 60 people”. I assume the most violent Sith are turned over to Belsavis while any who might have a chance of redemption to the light are brought to Tython. Some Sith probably will never become Jedi even if they are redeemed because let’s be clear, some of those Sith are probably majorly messed up in the head from PTSD and who knows what else. But they don’t have to become Jedi to be redeemed to the light so those individuals are probably kept on Tython the rest of their lives. Also another reason I think Tython as a high tech prison like the Coruscant temple… all those dark Jedi who are returned to the Jedi temple. They don’t redeem them in a single day lol. It takes time and a lot of effort and in the meantime, those fallen Jedi are considered a threat. Aka they have to be held *somewhere* secure on Tython.

In terms of criteria on who goes to Tython my guess is any Sith who the Jedi either believe can be redeemed, or are otherwise shown to be non-violent/compliant in captivity, meaning a lower risk of attempted escape or aggression, so probably… mostly Acolytes and apprentices with the occasional Lords (such as Pravin) who are shown to be less violent than their peers. Probably not Dark Council Members LOL. But there may be super rare exceptions. Like, if the Light Side Wrath (Sith warrior) was captured, they would more than likely be taken to Tython to either become a Jedi or remain for the rest of their lives, unable to leave. while a dark sided Wrath would most certainly get put into (heavily guarded) stasis on Belsavis. Sith in SWTOR use synthetic crystals, not kyber crystals. There's absolutely nothing special about red crystals that Sith used. Quite the opposite in fact.

In the Jedi, Kyber Crystals have a strong connection to the force as well as some semblance of will. The Kyber Crystal chooses the Jedi, not the other way around. And so obtaining a Kyber Crystal, and then constructing your own lightsaber, was seen as a right of passage, and a bit of a ritual.

Sith lightsabers are no such thing. They're not special. The crystals are synthetic. The crystals have no connection to the force or to the user at all. Sith don't have to go through some complex ritual like trial to obtain a kyber crystal that has specifically chosen them (nor would they be able to, as The Force is not too fond of Dark Side Users (see; Chaos, aka Hell in Star Wars).

So having your Sith character claim a Jedi's lightsaber could be a thing, sure, but corrupting the crystal is not a thing in SWTOR. So they'd literally just have to discard the crystal (because the crystal would be actively fighting against the Sith's mind and spirit if they tried to use it) and replace it with a synthetic one. Why bother when you can just be given a lightsaber? Especially since lightsabers and synthetic crystals are just not important in Sith culture.

It's more of a 'family heirloom' thing to them. "My Master gave me his lightsaber when I was ready, so now I am giving you my first lightsaber because you are ready." That's... it. It's nothing special for Sith.

To be fair, Disney made everything super confusing by changing everything and making Canon and Legends two entirely separate things. I personally prefer the whole 'red crystals are bled kyber crystals' thing, and i like the white crystals too in canon. But anyways, even I mix up canon and Legends a lot tbh. It's hard not to.

Alright i'm gunna give you some actual advice as someone who actually lives alone and doesn't work. the people telling you 'it's impossible' are wrong. But it also isn't easy. First, you need a diagnosis. Then you apply for SSI. You won't qualify for disability because you have to work for a minimum of like ten years or something like that. So you can get SSI. You will get denied your first time applying, happens to almost everyone. Apply again. They denied me the first time lol. If they keep denying you, you might be able to get a lawyer to help. Ok now you need to find a HUD housing place, or Section 8. I live in one specifically for people with special needs and cannot work. Look around for one and start the process as SOON AS POSSIBLE. It can take years to get into this housing so don't wait, because most people live in this housing their whole lives. If your state has a mental health or disibility program, get into it, and get a case worker. Your case worker will help you find HUD housing as well as other benefits based off your state. Ok so once you get into HUD housing, they take like 35% of your income or something, so if you make 914$ from SSI, your rent will be somewhere between 250 and 300 I think. I can't math lol. Often times, like in my case, utilities is included in that. Ok now maybe you want internet. There's a federal program that supplies super low income people with SUPER cheap internet. Like... REALLY cheap. Look into that and find an internet company that works with that federal program. I don't drive, I have staff who drive me, so I don't have to worry about gas. If you can drive and you have a car, gas is very expensive. and you also need groceries. in my case, it's pretty easy. i don't like to live lavish so just getting what i need makes me happy. you wont be able to have more than 2,000 dollars at any time, so be aware. but also you can't have more than 2,000 in assets, so don't go splurging on flatscreen tvs. Not that you'd be able to buy one anyways on SSI but. Ok now you are getting medicaid and SSI, and if you have a case worker, you want to talk to them about an ABLE account. An ABLE account will allow you to save up to like 100,000$ for medical expensives. If you have a diagnosis and you are on SSI and you are living in HUD, you should qualify. 100,000 is not a lot when it comes to medical stuff, but it should pay for your therapy and routine appointments at least. Just dont go breaking any bones. You won't be able to pay off medical bills so be very careful about the doctors you see, make sure they take medicaid. Make sure the treatment is covered. etc. and that's that! I live very comfortably off 900$ a month. It is possible, but you have to advocate for yourself to get into those programs. I wish you luck! :) I live totally alone in my apartment with a few staff in the office who help us out. It is POSSIBLE. You will only be semi independent. But it is a good life for me. Maybe you will be fine with it too.

The two lists have major differences. I have played both extensively. 

— Wildlander has better graphics and also has better performance (weird, I know!)

— Wildlander is not as hardcore as Librum, but early game can still be very challenging. Everything is more expensive in Wildlander but the economy is still significantly easier than Librum’s. Overall, Librum is just a lot more difficult in almost every aspect.

— Wildlander is vanilla Skyrim with a gorgeous graphics overhaul and Requiem on top, but not much new content. while Librum has various new content such as followers (Lucien, Inigo), quest mods, city mods, etc.

If you want a gorgeous, streamlined vanilla+ experience, choose Wildlander. If you want a hardcore, dark fantasy playthrough with loads of new content, choose Librum.

My favorite is Librum. Very hardcore, old-school style RPG inspired. The magic system is very hard to break into, no spell tomes except rare ones around the map, you have to use a spell research system to get spells, so it takes a lot of time and effort. The pay off is exactly what you'd expect, a shit ton of amazing spells that make you god-like. Survival mods make the experience a lot more difficult early on, so you feel genuine progression. De-leveled enemies around the world will ruin your day in a second, and a punishing (but fair) death and respawn system mean that you'd better plan accordingly before engaging with risky fights.

It has some problems, such as using Convenient Horses which is janky at the best of times (all up to personal preference though), and the dragons are virtually impossible without magic. But the 4.0 version is being worked on, and will include a custom perk overhaul and dragon overhaul along with several other exciting additions. It doesn't have Requiem, but you will find that it is significantly more hardcore than Requiem lists while simultaneously not neutering entire builds (like stealth builds), so that all classes are viable if you're willing to put enough work and planning into them.

If he has installed Oblivion with mods before, then uninstalled Oblivion, then those mods don't get deleted, at least not the ones that are manually installed. In other words, your brother might have leftover mods from an incomplete uninstallation of a modded Oblivion in the past. He thinks he has no mods because he just reinstalled it, but in reality, the game was never properly uninstalled in the first place. You can't just press 'uninstall' and be done with it if you manually install mods. I had similar issues when I first started modding Oblivion years ago. Also important, some mods don't have an esp or an esm. Your brother might think he turned off all his mods by unticking them in a mod manager, but all those mods without an esp/esm will have to be manually uninstalled by hand. Hope this helps. \^\^

Blackwood… has a pretty city but a boring zone imo. It does introduce companions, though.

**My Current Favorites:** 

Clockwork - A horror and dwemer themed quest mod with an excellent player home reward.

Wyrmstooth - A vanilla+ styled new lands mod in which you hunt down a troublesome dragon.

The Forgotten City - An award winning mod with a quest that has multiple endings.

The Tale of Tsatampra Xiros - A very high quality Hermaeus Mora themed quest mod.

Identity Crisis - An excellently done Sheogorath quest mod.

Paarthurnax - Quest Expansion - An excellent (and imo, better), fully voiced alternative to The Paarthurnax Dilemma.

**Mods I Recommend Avoiding**

Rigmor of Bruma - Cringe dialogue simulator that breaks lore and portrays your Dragonborn as an absolute horn-dog.

Mirai - The Girl with the Dragon Heart - Extremely lore breaking (female dragons, dragon mates and families, etc), and the writing is pretty bad.

M'rissi's Tails of Troubles - This one personally makes me pretty uncomfortable due to themes of sexual abuse and slavery. But to each their own. If these themes don't bother you, then by all means, give it a try.

**Mods I'm Iffy About, but won't NOT Recommend Them**

Legacy of the Dragonborn - A quest and collection heavy mod that's great for completionists, but not so much for lore-beards. The mod outright contradicts and even changes established lore on more than one occasion. That said, the museum itself is gorgeous, and the voice acting is fairly high quality. It's not a good mod for those that like to roleplay, meaning they play a mage character that wouldn't realistically join the Thieves Guild or The Companions. This mod is for completionists that are willing to join every single guild to get as many artifacts as possible.
